assertion: Remote client creation is demand-driven and distinct from startup-managed daemon control.
Raw TCP without application TLS must not be represented as verified peer identity.
Optional client token and required server authentication are tested as distinct states.
Queue-send and response deadlines have separate acceptance states and pending cleanup.
Response timeout after server execution remains unknown acceptance and forbids blind resend.
Only exact disconnect errors trigger one allowlisted retry; writes are not generally replayable.
Runtime-args/connect/resume/live retries need method-level idempotence or reconciliation.
Invalid JSON, unknown shapes and unmatched IDs are diagnosed without fabricated completion.
Only three bridged notification kinds do not establish parity for every OS event.
Disconnect draining does not collapse unsent, partially sent and executed requests into one fact.
WSL UNC normalization must retain explicit target-machine/distro identity rather than silently broadening paths.
Loopback standalone and all-interface managed listeners are separate sealing entries.
No-token dev mode, unauthorized requests and authenticated event subscription are independently checked.
Malformed or ID-less requests retain diagnostic policy even when no error response is possible.
Per-connection concurrency limits do not imply per-session execution order.
Slow clients cannot create unbounded response/event memory without an explicit budget.
Broadcast lag requires gap/cursor/snapshot handling rather than silently continuing.
No event receivers is not durable delivery; producer send failure remains observable.
Client EOF aborts transport tasks but does not falsely certify cancellation of spawned business work.
Shutdown acknowledgment precedes 100ms process exit and must not impersonate drained writers.
Daemon no-op menus and daemon-host notification fallback are explicitly non-equivalent to desktop UX.
Initial invalid settings/workspaces must fail closed instead of authorizing an empty writer state.
Missing HOME/XDG must not construct a cwd-relative standalone daemon root.
Managed --data-dir must identify the same canonical product root and actual lock owner.
List-triggered stale pruning must not kill a shared Arc still referenced by a surviving workspace.
Subsequent storage read failure retains stale memory but must report staleness, unlike successful empty load.
Pruned map membership is not proof that the removed native writer has stopped.
Daemon file canonicalization, UTF-8 and 400k limits apply independently of public Files policy.
Startup remote and local-existing-daemon branches are both sealed while retaining local-host capability.
Settings save cannot silently start/restart a sealed remote daemon.
Exit stop/keep setting must not equate app exit with daemon or child-tree termination.
Command preview uses placeholders and does not expose token or claim a process was started.
Preflight token/binary/root/listener probes are separate from actual bind/readiness.
Version mismatch restart requires ownership/auth before attempting shutdown or signals.
PID from daemon info or listener tooling is insufficient without creation-time identity.
Token in daemon argv is a local process-inspection exposure and requires a protected launch channel.
Spawn-success Running status must be reconciled with actual bind/auth/ping readiness.
Managed child kill/wait and subsequent probe retain distinct failures.
External daemon force-stop remains ownership-guarded and verifies the final listener state.
Tailscale probe uses the correctly spelled binary and macOS launchctl/direct fallback identities.
Tailnet/DNS/host/IP diagnostics remain private external identity, not public migration content.
Daemonctl platform home fallbacks cannot create a relative product root.
Argument, environment and settings token precedence must preserve secrecy and selected identity.
Status probes network; start/stop mutate processes and cannot evade sealing via the CLI entry.
Configured mobile wizard auto-test is blocked independently of its visible Connect button.
Failed mobile connection leaves first saved remote config; restore must not reactivate it.
React/settings/profile token copies are individually excluded from ordinary export and migration.
